book_questions.question_en:
Which of the following statements about India's
foreign policy are true?
A. India has signed the Land Boundary Agreement (LBA)
with Bangladesh in 2015
B. India has agreed to build Hambantota port in Sri Lanka
in 2017
C. India has signed a Strategic Partnership Agreement
(SPA) with Afghanistan in 2011
D. The regime of Abdulla Yameen (2013-2018) of Maldives
was friendly with India
book_questions.explanation_en:
Statement (A) is true; the historic Land
Boundary Agreement was ratified in 2015. Statement (C) is
also true; India and Afghanistan signed the SPA in 2011.
However, (B) is false; China, not India, developed the
Hambantota port. (D) is also false; the Yameen regime in
Maldives was known for its pro-China stance and strained
relations with India.

book_questions.question_en:
Arrange the signing of the following agreements by
India in order of their appearance:
A. Land Boundary Agreement
B. Tashkent Agreement
C. Moscow Test Ban Treaty
D. India-Russia Friendship Treaty
book_questions.explanation_en:
The chronological order is as follows: India
signed the Moscow Test Ban Treaty (Partial Test Ban
Treaty) in 1963 (C), the Tashkent Agreement with Pakistan
in 1966 (B), the Indo-Soviet Treaty of Peace, Friendship and
Cooperation (often referred to as the friendship treaty) in
1971 (D), and ratified the Land Boundary Agreement with
Bangladesh in 2015 (A).

book_questions.question_en:
Who wrote the book "The India Way: Strategies for an
Uncertain World"?
book_questions.explanation_en:
"The India Way" (2020) is a highly influential
book written by Dr. S. Jaishankar, the current Minister of
External Affairs of India. In this book, he outlines his vision
for India's foreign policy in a multipolar, uncertain world,
emphasizing pragmatism and the need to move beyond
traditional non-alignment. Other options: Sunil Khilnani is
known for 'The Idea of India'. C. Raja Mohan and Sumit
Ganguly are prominent academic scholars of Indian foreign
policy and security.

book_questions.question_en:
Jawaharlal Nehru became the first Prime Minister of
India in 1947. Events under Nehru's leadership includes:
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
A. The National Planning Commission appointed Nehru
as its Chairman in 1950.
B. Nehru visited China in 1958 and Signed the Panch-
Sheel Treaty.
C. Nehru fought three general elections.
D. In 1952 the first of the five IIT's was set up.
E. India signed a treaty with Nepal in 1950.
book_questions.explanation_en:
Analyzing the historical events: A is True: The
Planning Commission was set up in March 1950 with PM
Nehru as its first chairman. B is False: The Panchsheel
Agreement (Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence) was
signed between India and China in 1954, not 1958. C is
True: Nehru led the Congress party to victory in the first
three general elections (1952, 1957, and 1962). D is True:
The first Indian Institute of Technology (IIT Kharagpur) was
formally inaugurated in the early 1950s (1951/52). E is True:
The Indo-Nepal Treaty of Peace and Friendship was signed
in July 1950.

focus: India-China relations: Panchsheel, boundary question and historical turning points
title: India's Foreign Policy - Practice 06

book_questions.question_en: Name the boundary line between India and China
book_questions.explanation_en:
The McMahon Line is the effective boundary
between the eastern part of India and China. The Radcliffe
Line is the boundary between India and Pakistan, and the
Durand Line is between Pakistan and Afghanistan. The Palk
Strait is the body of water separating India and Sri Lanka.

book_questions.question_en:
Which of the following statements are correct?
(A) India and China are neighbours
(B) There is a border dispute between India and China
(C) China is not a nuclear power
(D) China has supported India's quest for permanent
membership of UNSC
book_questions.explanation_en:
India and China share a long border (A) and
have an ongoing and unresolved border dispute (B). China
is a recognized nuclear power (C is incorrect) and has
consistently blocked India's bid for a permanent seat on
the UNSC (D is incorrect).

book_questions.question_en:
Which of the following is correctly matched.
(A) Hydropower Diplomacy - India- Nepal
(B) Basic Group – China
(C) Group of 77-USA
(D) BIMSTEC- Pakistan
book_questions.explanation_en:
India and Nepal have significant cooperation
in the hydropower sector (A). The BASIC group of countries
on climate change includes Brazil, South Africa, India, and
China (B). The USA is not a member of the G77 (which is a
coalition of developing nations) (C). Pakistan is not a
member of BIMSTEC (D).

book_questions.question_en:
Which of the following is correctly matched
(A) War on Terrorism-USA
(B) Maritime Silk Road India
(C) Viktor Yanukovych Ukraine
(D) Line of Control - China
book_questions.explanation_en:
The "War on Terrorism" was a foreign policy
doctrine initiated by the USA after the 9/11 attacks (A).
Viktor Yanukovych was a former President of Ukraine (C).
The Maritime Silk Road is a Chinese initiative (part of the
Belt and Road Initiative), not Indian (B is incorrect). The
Line of Control (LoC) refers to the military control line
between India and Pakistan in Jammu and Kashmir, not
with China (D is incorrect).

focus: India and South Asian neighbours: SAARC, Gujral Doctrine and bilateral policy
title: India's Foreign Policy - Practice 07

book_questions.question_en:
In India's Foreign Policy, 'Indira Doctrine' is related
to
A. It aims to make India a global power
B. It is a policy to develop cooperation with neighbours
C. It equates India's security with that of South Asia
D. Any interference in the South Asian region will be
considered a threat to India's security
book_questions.explanation_en:
The Indira Doctrine, which emerged in the
early 1980s, established India's security perimeter in South
Asia. It asserts that India's security is synonymous with the
security of the entire region (C) and that the intervention of
external powers in the region would be considered a threat
to India's own security (D), which India would not tolerate.

book_questions.question_en:
Which of the following is correctly matched.
(A) SAARC Kathmandu
(B) Act East Policy - Narasimha Rao
(C) Neighbourhood first policy - Narendra Modi
(D) Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank Kualalampur
book_questions.explanation_en:
The SAARC Secretariat is headquartered in
Kathmandu, Nepal (A). The "Neighbourhood First" policy is
a cornerstone of the foreign policy of the Narendra Modi
government (C). The "Act East Policy" is a successor to the
"Look East Policy" (initiated by Narasimha Rao), but it was
launched by the Modi government (B is incorrect). The
headquarters of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank
(AIIB) is in Beijing, not Kuala Lumpur (D is incorrect).

book_questions.question_en:
Arrange the following events of Indian Foreign
Policy in order of their occurrence
A. Lahore Bus Diplomacy
B. Look East Policy
C. Gujral Doctrine
D. Pokhran-II Nuclear Explosion
book_questions.explanation_en:
The chronological sequence of these foreign
policy events is: Look East Policy (articulated in the early
1990s by P.V. Narasimha Rao), Gujral Doctrine (1996),
Pokhran-II nuclear tests (May 1998), and the Lahore Bus
Diplomacy initiative (February 1999).

book_questions.question_en:
Para Diplomacy is/was part of India's Foreign Policy
under
book_questions.explanation_en:
Para-diplomacy, which refers to international
relations conducted by sub-national governments (like
states), has been actively encouraged under the Narendra
Modi government as part of a broader strategy to engage
with the world, particularly for attracting investment and
fostering cultural ties.

focus: Look East/Act East and India-ASEAN relations: chronology and objectives
title: India's Foreign Policy - Practice 08

book_questions.question_en:
During whose government the look East policy was
adopted?
book_questions.explanation_en:
India's "Look East" policy was initiated in the
early 1990s under the government of Prime Minister P.V.
Narasimha Rao to strengthen economic and strategic
relations with Southeast Asian nations.

book_questions.question_en:
Which American President delivered following
statement about India "I think it is really very sad that 600
million people have lost what they had since the mid-
1940's. I hope that in time there could be a restoration of
democratic processes as we know them in the US"?
book_questions.explanation_en:
US President Gerald Ford made this
statement in response to the imposition of the National
Emergency in India in 1975 by Prime Minister Indira
Gandhi. The suspension of fundamental rights, jailing of
political opposition, and press censorship drew sharp
criticism from the West. Ford expressed sorrow that the
democratic rights the Indian populace had enjoyed since
independence in 1947 ("the mid-1940s") had been
suspended.

book_questions.question_en:
In September 2000, the Government of India had set
up a high level Committee on the Indian Diaspora under
the Chairmanship of-
book_questions.explanation_en:
In September 2000, the NDA government led
by PM Atal Bihari Vajpayee constituted a High-Level
Committee on the Indian Diaspora under the chairmanship
of Dr. L.M. Singhvi (an eminent jurist and diplomat). The
committee's mandate was to study the global Indian
diaspora and recommend policies to foster closer ties. A
major outcome of this committee's recommendations was
the institution of the Pravasi Bharatiya Divas (celebrated
annually on January 9) and the PIO (Persons of Indian
Origin) card scheme.

book_questions.question_en:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as
Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A: The Tashkent Declaration was signed by
President Ayub Khan of Pakistan and Lal Bahadur Shastri
Prime Minister of India on January 10, 1966.
Reason R: The Tashkent Declaration was meant to form a
framework for lasting peace between India and Pakistan.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most
appropriate answer from the options given below:
options_en:
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct
explanation of A

Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct
explanation of A
A is correct but R is not correct
A is not correct but R is correct
book_questions.explanation_en:
Assertion (A) is historically accurate.
Following the Indo-Pakistani War of 1965, the Tashkent
Declaration was signed on January 10, 1966, in the Soviet
Union (modern-day Uzbekistan). Reason (R) is also correct
and explains the intent behind A. Mediated by Soviet
Premier Aleksei Kosygin, the explicit goal of the treaty was
to restore the status quo ante bellum (forcing both armies
to withdraw to pre-war lines) and to establish a diplomatic
framework for "lasting peace" and normalized bilateral
relations.

focus: India and West Asia, Africa and the Indian diaspora: stable policy frameworks
title: India's Foreign Policy - Practice 09

book_questions.question_en:
Why debate on Indian diaspora got prominence for
India's foreign policy makers?
options_en: Due to changed political milieu in the USA
India's economic thrust towards West Asia
Compulsions of the Globalization process in India
book_questions.explanation_en:
The passage highlights that developments
within diaspora communities, particularly the creation of
GOPIO and the India Caucus, drove the renewed policy
debate. This points to a resurgence and increased
organization and political consciousness among the Indian
diaspora itself, making them more significant actors for
Indian foreign policy.

book_questions.question_en:
Which of the following is NOT provided to the
Indian diaspora under the 'Overseas Citizenship of India
(OCI) scheme'?
book_questions.explanation_en:
The OCI scheme grants the Indian diaspora
several rights, including a lifelong visa and parity with NRIs
in economic and educational fields. However, OCI
cardholders do not have political rights in India; they
cannot vote, hold public office, or be appointed to
government posts.

book_questions.question_en:
What is the name of the exercise project initiated by
India to link Indian Ocean Rim Countries?
book_questions.explanation_en:
Project Mausam is a cultural and diplomatic
initiative by the Indian government to reconnect and re-
establish communications and historical ties between
countries of the Indian Ocean world.

book_questions.question_en:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as
Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A: British Viceroy Lord Curzon stated in 1901
that it would be madness for us to cross the Himalayas and
occupy Tibet.
Reason R: This British policy in a very big way helped the
Chinese to re-establish their hold over Tibet during 1905-
1911.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most
appropriate answer from the options given below:
options_en:
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct
explanation of A

Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct
explanation of A
A is correct but R is not correct
A is not correct but R is correct
book_questions.explanation_en:
Assertion (A) is correct. Initially, Lord Curzon
believed that fully occupying and administering Tibet
across the Himalayas would be a logistical and financial
"madness" for the British Indian Empire (though he later
sent the Younghusband expedition in 1903-04 strictly to
counter Russian influence, not to annex). Reason (R) is
correct and explains the consequence. By actively deciding
not to integrate Tibet into the British Empire and instead
formally recognizing Chinese "suzerainty" over the region
(to act as a buffer state), the British effectively paved the
way for the waning Qing Dynasty to aggressively re-assert
its control over Lhasa between 1905 and 1911.

focus: India and EU, BRICS, SCO and multilateral diplomacy; historical foundations
title: India's Foreign Policy - Practice 10

book_questions.question_en:
Who wrote the book "Engaging India: Diplomacy,
Democracy and the Bomb" ?
book_questions.explanation_en:
Engaging India: Diplomacy, Democracy, and
the Bomb was written by Strobe Talbott, an American
diplomat who served as the Deputy Secretary of State from
1994 to 2001. The book provides an insider's account of
the extensive diplomatic dialogues between the United
States and India following India's 1998 nuclear tests.

book_questions.question_en:
Which of the following statements are correct?
(A) India conducted its first nuclear test in 1974
(B) India considers NPT as discriminatory
(C) India is a signatory to CTBT
(D) India is not a member of Nuclear Supplier's Group
(E) India is a signatory to NPT
book_questions.explanation_en:
India's first nuclear test was in 1974 (A). India
has consistently viewed the NPT as discriminatory (B) and
is not a member of the NSG (D) due to its non-signatory
status on the NPT. India has not signed the CTBT or the
NPT (C and E are incorrect).

book_questions.question_en:
Choose the correct statements from the following.
(A) India is a signatory to Chemical Weapons Convention
(CWC)
(B) India is a signatory to Biological Weapons Convention
(BWC)
(C) India is not a member of Missile Technology Control
Regime (MTCR)
(D) India is a member of Wassenaar Arrangement
(E) India is a member of Australia Group
book_questions.explanation_en:
India is a signatory to both the CWC (A) and
BWC (B). It is also a member of the Wassenaar
Arrangement (D) and the Australia Group (E). India became
a member of the MTCR in 2016, so statement (C) is
incorrect.

book_questions.question_en:
When open skies agreement between India and USA
was signed?
book_questions.explanation_en:
The India-US Open Skies Agreement,
allowing for unrestricted air services by the airlines of both
countries, was signed on April 14, 2005.

focus: India at UN, WTO, IMF and climate negotiations: positions and institutional roles
title: India's Foreign Policy - Practice 11

book_questions.question_en:
Match the LIST-I (Individual) with LIST-II (Positions
Held):
LIST-I LIST-II
I. Chairman of the
A. K.P.S Menon United Nations
Commission on
II. Chairman of the
B. Justice Fazl Ali
Neutral Nations
III. Chairman of the
C. General K.S. Thimayya
States
IV. The President of the
D. Nalini Ranjan Sarkar
Federation of
book_questions.explanation_en:
The correct pairings are: K.P.S. Menon, a
distinguished diplomat, served as the Chairman of the UN
Commission on Korea. Justice Fazl Ali was the Chairman of
the States Reorganisation Commission, which
recommended the reorganization of Indian states along
linguistic lines. General K.S. Thimayya served as the
Chairman of the Neutral Nations Repatriation Commission
after the Korean War. Nalini Ranjan Sarkar was a prominent
industrialist who served as the President of FICCI.
: Source: UGC NET June 2025

book_questions.question_en:
Which of the following is correctly matched
(A) Civil liability of Nuclear Damages Act-2010
(B) India - US ten year frame work Agreement for Defence
Co-operation – 2015
(C) Defence Technology and Trade Initiative - 2020
(D) Basic Exchange Co-operations Agreement 2019
book_questions.explanation_en:
The Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act
was passed by the Indian Parliament in 2010 (A). The 10-
year Defence Framework Agreement between India and
the US was renewed in 2015 (B). The Defence Technology
and Trade Initiative (DTTI) was launched in 2012, not 2020
(C is incorrect). The Basic Exchange and Cooperation
Agreement (BECA) was signed in 2020, not 2019 (D is
incorrect).

book_questions.question_en:
In 1954, India signed the Panchsheel agreement with
which neighboring state?
book_questions.explanation_en:
The Panchsheel, or the Five Principles of
Peaceful Coexistence, was an agreement signed between
India and the People's Republic of China in 1954. It was
intended to govern the relations between the two
countries, though the principles were later violated.

book_questions.question_en:
Which one of the following is NOT a feature of
India's 'Nuclear Doctrine'?
options_en: Not against a state having conventional weapons only
book_questions.explanation_en:
India's nuclear doctrine is based on "credible
minimum deterrence" and a "no first use" (NFU) policy. The
NFU implies that India will only use nuclear weapons in
retaliation against a nuclear attack. The statement "No use
against friendly countries" is not a formal feature; the
doctrine's focus is on adversaries and conditions of
retaliation.

focus: Maritime, energy, environmental, cyber and water security: foreign-policy applications
title: India's Foreign Policy - Practice 12

book_questions.question_en:
Which Prime Minister pursued the foreign policy of
extending non-reciprocal concessions to neighbouring
states?
book_questions.explanation_en:
This policy is the cornerstone of the 'Gujral
Doctrine', named after Inder Kumar Gujral, who was
Foreign Minister and later Prime Minister. The doctrine
advocates that India, as the larger country, should extend
unilateral concessions to its smaller neighbours without
expecting reciprocity, in the interest of building trust and
regional cooperation.

book_questions.question_en: Project Mausam is a policy linked with
book_questions.explanation_en:
Project Mausam is a cultural and diplomatic
initiative by the Indian government aimed at reconnecting
and re-establishing historical and cultural linkages with the
countries of the Indian Ocean region.

book_questions.question_en:
Peaceful Nuclear Explosion (PNE) was a policy of the
Government under?
book_questions.explanation_en:
India's first nuclear test in 1974, codenamed
"Smiling Buddha," was officially declared a Peaceful
Nuclear Explosion (PNE). This occurred during the prime
ministership of Indira Gandhi.

book_questions.question_en:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as
Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A: Pakistani Parliament has voted to give its
army chief new powers and lifetime immunity from arrest
and persecution.
Reason R: Judiciary is very weak in Pakistan.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most
appropriate answer from the options given below:
options_en:
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct
explanation of A

Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct
explanation of A
A is correct but R is not correct
A is not correct but R is correct
book_questions.explanation_en:
Assertion (A) is correct, referring to recent
amendments to the Pakistan Army Act that grant the
military and its leadership sweeping protections against
prosecution and further consolidate their power. Reason
(R) is also correct and provides the structural explanation
for A. The historic and ongoing weakness, and often
compliance, of Pakistan's judiciary and civilian
governments is exactly what allows the military
establishment to extract such sweeping legal immunities
and maintain its dominance over the state's political
apparatus.

focus: Constitution making: colonial heritage, national movement and Constituent Assembly
title: Political Institutions in India - Practice 01

book_questions.question_en:
For which purpose was the Cabinet Mission sent to
India?
A. To establish a national government
B. To workout a constitutional arrangement for the transfer
of power
C. To suppress the intensity of the national movement
D. A Constituent Assembly to be elected by Provincial
Assemblies through proportional representation
book_questions.explanation_en:
The Cabinet Mission of 1946 was sent to
India with three main objectives: to help form an interim
national government (A), to devise a constitutional
arrangement for the transfer of power (B), and to establish
a mechanism for framing the constitution, which was the
Constituent Assembly (D). Suppressing the national
movement (C) was not its objective.

book_questions.question_en:
Who remarked that the goal of Indian Constitution
drafted by the Constituent Assembly was entirely political
and not at all social or economic?
book_questions.explanation_en:
British constitutional scholar Ivor Jennings
critically viewed the Indian Constitution primarily as a
political document and argued that its objectives were
essentially political rather than being directly aimed at
social or economic transformation.

book_questions.question_en:
Which of the following are associated with the
national movement of India?
A. The Khilafat Movement
B. All Parties Conference Committee Report
C. Bombay Accord
D. Poona Pact
E. Cripps Mission
Choose the correct answer:
book_questions.explanation_en:
The Khilafat Movement, the All Parties
Conference/Committee Report, the Poona Pact (1932)
and the Cripps Mission (1942) are all important
developments associated with India's national movement.
The Bombay Accord is not included among these major
national-movement developments in the context of this
question. Therefore, the correct combination is A, B, D and
E. The Poona Pact provided reserved seats for the
Depressed Classes within a joint electorate.

book_questions.question_en:
Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected President of the
Constituent Assembly on-
book_questions.explanation_en:
The Constituent Assembly of India held its
first meeting on 9 December 1946. Following the French
practice, the oldest member, Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha,
was elected as the temporary/interim President. Two days
later, on 11 December 1946, the Assembly formally and
unanimously elected Dr. Rajendra Prasad as its permanent
President, alongside H.C. Mukherjee as the Vice-President.

focus: Preamble, constitutional philosophy, citizenship and fundamental duties
title: Political Institutions in India - Practice 02

book_questions.question_en:
Arrange the following in the chronological order of
their addition through amendments to the Constitution of
India:
(A) The Right to Property was removed from the list of
Fundamental Rights.
(B) A new chapter on Fundamental Duties of citizens was
added.
(C) Creation of the state of Meghalaya.
(D) The privy purses and privileges of the rulers of the
Indian states were abolished.
(E) The Union Territory of Arunachal Pradesh was granted
statehood.
book_questions.explanation_en:
The correct chronological order of these
events is: (C) Creation of Meghalaya: 22nd Amendment,
1969 (D) Abolition of Privy Purses: 26th Amendment, 1971
(B) Addition of Fundamental Duties: 42nd Amendment,
1976 (A) Removal of Right to Property: 44th Amendment,
1978 (E) Statehood for Arunachal Pradesh: 55th
Amendment, 1986

book_questions.question_en:
The Citizenship Act prescribes the following ways for
acquisition of citizenship of India:
A. By birth
B. By registration if a person is married to a citizen of India
C. By descent if either of his/her parents is a citizen of India
at the time of the person's birth
D. By descent if either of his/her grandparents were citizens
of India at the time of Partition
E. By recommendation from President of India
Choose the correct answer:
book_questions.explanation_en:
The Citizenship Act provides acquisition of
citizenship by birth, descent, registration, naturalisation
and incorporation of territory. A person may acquire
citizenship by registration subject to statutory conditions,
including certain provisions relating to spouses of Indian
citizens. Citizenship is not acquired merely because a
grandparent was an Indian citizen at Partition, nor is there
a general route through recommendation of the President.

book_questions.question_en:
Which of the following words were added to the
Preamble of the Constitution of India through the Forty-
Second Amendment Act?
options_en: Unity and integrity of the nation
book_questions.explanation_en:
The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act,
1976 added the words “Socialist” and “Secular” to the
description of India in the Preamble. It also changed “unity
of the nation” to “unity and integrity of the nation.”
Therefore, among the given options, option (3) represents
the words added through the 42nd Amendment.

book_questions.question_en:
W. H. Morris Jones has termed the Indian
constitutional system as:
book_questions.explanation_en:
W. H. Morris-Jones described Indian
federalism as “bargaining federalism.” He used this
expression to highlight the importance of negotiation and
bargaining between the Union and the States. Indian
federalism does not operate as a completely rigid division
of powers; instead, political relations often involve
accommodation, negotiation and adjustment between
different levels of government. This makes bargaining an
important feature of Indian federal practice

focus: Fundamental Rights: scope, protections and established constitutional interpretations
title: Political Institutions in India - Practice 03

book_questions.question_en:
The Indian constitution ensures individual freedom
by
(A) Limiting the power of Government.
(B) Laying down relations between the State and
individuals by demanding their powers rights respective.
(C) Defining civil rights and liberties.
(D) Recognizing the fundamental rights of people.
(E) No guaranteeing for the delivery of rights.
book_questions.explanation_en:
The Indian Constitution secures individual
freedom through several mechanisms. It establishes a
system of limited government (A), defines the relationship
and demarcates powers between the state and individuals
(B), explicitly defines civil rights and liberties (C), and
recognizes these as enforceable Fundamental Rights (D).
Statement (E) is incorrect; the Constitution, particularly
through the right to constitutional remedies (Article 32),
guarantees the delivery and protection of these rights.

book_questions.question_en:
Which of the following rights are declared as
Fundamental rights under Article 21 of the Indian
Constitution?
(A) Right against public Hanging
(B) Right to sustainable development
(C) Right to Livelihood
(D) Right to Free education up to 16 years of age
(E) Right to Reputation
options_en: A, B, C, D and E only
A, B, C and E only
book_questions.explanation_en:
The Supreme Court has interpreted Article 21
to include rights like the right against public hanging (A),
sustainable development (B), livelihood (C), and reputation
(E). The Right to Free Education is under Article 21A and
applies up to the age of 14, not 16.

book_questions.question_en:
Which one of the following fundamental rights are
provided, to both citizens and non-citizens?
book_questions.explanation_en:
The Right to Equality (Article 14), which
guarantees equality before the law, is available to all
persons, including citizens and non-citizens. The other
rights listed are either exclusively for citizens (like Article
16, part of equal opportunity) or have specific restrictions
for non-citizens.

book_questions.question_en: Five Zonal Councils were established through the:
options_en: Efforts of the Chief Minister's conference
Legislation passed during the first NDA regime
book_questions.explanation_en:
The five Zonal Councils were established
under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956. They were
created to promote cooperation and coordination among
states and to address common regional issues.

focus: Directive Principles and their relationship with rights and welfare commitments
title: Political Institutions in India - Practice 04

book_questions.question_en:
Arrange the following Directive Principles of State
Policy in their sequential order as mentioned in the
constitution
(A) To organize village Panchayat
(B) To secure the right to work
(C) To make provision for just and humane condition
(D) To secure a living wage, decent standard of life
book_questions.explanation_en:
The correct sequence of these articles is:
Article 40 (A), Article 41 (B), Article 42 (C), and Article 43
(D).

book_questions.question_en:
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II:
LIST-I LIST-II
A. Cooperative Federalism I. K. C. Wheare
B. Bargaining Federalism II. Granville Austin
C. Quasi-Federalism III. NITI Aayog
D. Competitive Federalism IV. Morris Jones
Choose the correct answer:
book_questions.explanation_en:
Granville Austin is associated with
cooperative federalism; Morris Jones developed the idea
of bargaining federalism; K. C. Wheare described the
Indian Constitution as quasi-federal; and NITI Aayog
promotes competitive federalism.

book_questions.question_en:
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II:
LIST-I LIST-II
A. Reservation of seats for Scheduled
I. Article 243-I
Castes and Tribes in Municipality
B. Finance Commission in relation to
II. Article 16(4)
Panchayats
C. Reservation in favour of backward III. Article 243-
classes T
D. Special provisions for the IV. Article
protection of women and children 15(3)
Choose the correct answer:
book_questions.explanation_en:
Article 243-T deals with reservation of seats
for SCs and STs in municipalities. Article 243-I provides for
the State Finance Commission for Panchayats. Article 16(4)
enables reservation in favour of backward classes. Article
15(3) permits special provisions for women and children.
Hence, the correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.

book_questions.question_en:
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II:
LIST-I LIST-II
A. Borrowing by states I. Article 143
B. Inter-State Council II. Article 293
C. Official language of Union III. Article 263

D. Presidential reference IV. Article 343
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
book_questions.explanation_en:
Article 293 deals with borrowing by States;
Article 263 provides for the Inter-State Council; Article 343
deals with the official language of the Union; and Article
143 concerns the President’s power to seek the Supreme
Court’s advisory opinion. Therefore, A-II, B-III, C-IV and D-I
is correct.

focus: Amendment procedures, basic structure and constitutional judicial decisions
title: Political Institutions in India - Practice 05

book_questions.question_en: "Basic Structure" is outcome of :
book_questions.explanation_en:
The "Basic Structure" doctrine is not
mentioned in the Constitution. It is a legal principle that
evolved through judicial interpretation, most notably laid
down by the Supreme Court in the landmark Kesavananda
Bharati v. State of Kerala case in 1973.

book_questions.question_en:
By which Constitutional Amendment Act,
Maintenance of Internal Security Act (MISA) removed from
the 9th schedule ?
book_questions.explanation_en:
The Maintenance of Internal Security Act
(MISA) was placed in the 9th Schedule by the 39th
Amendment during the Emergency to shield it from
judicial review. The post-Emergency Janata Party
government enacted the 44th Amendment in 1978, which,
among other changes, removed MISA from the 9th
Schedule.

book_questions.question_en:
Which of the following are the common
compulsory provisions of the 73rd and 74th Constitutional
Amendment Act?
A. Five-yearly elections
B. Reservation for Backward Classes
C. Reservation for women
D. Nagar Panchayats
book_questions.explanation_en:
Both the 73rd (Panchayats) and 74th
(Municipalities) amendments have compulsory provisions
for a five-year term and regular elections (A) and
reservation of not less than one-third of the seats for
women (C). Reservation for Backward Classes (B) is a
voluntary/enabling provision left to the discretion of state
legislatures. Nagar Panchayats (D) are specific to the 74th
Amendment.

book_questions.question_en:
Which of the following are provided for by the 74th
Constitutional Amendment in respect of Municipal
Corporation?
A. Seats to be filled by direct elections on the basis of
wards
B. Reservation of seats for Scheduled castes and Scheduled
tribe
C. Reservation of seats for backward classes
D. One-third reservation of seats for women
book_questions.explanation_en:
The 74th Amendment Act provides for direct
elections to fill seats in municipalities (A), reservation of
seats for SCs and STs in proportion to their population (B),
and reservation of not less than one-third of the total seats
for women (D). While it allows state legislatures to make
provisions for reserving seats for Backward Classes (C), it is

book_questions.question_en:
Which British Prime Minister stated about Jallianwala
Bagh massacre that it was "utterably Monstrous"?
book_questions.explanation_en:
On July 8, 1920, during a debate in the
House of Commons regarding the Hunter Commission's
report on the Amritsar massacre, Winston Churchill (then
Secretary of State for War, later Prime Minister) strongly
condemned General Dyer's actions. He famously described
the Jallianwala Bagh massacre as "an episode which
appears to me to be without precedent or parallel... an
extraordinary event, a monstrous event."

book_questions.question_en:
According to the rules of the Lok Sabha, identify the
correct statements regarding Parliamentary Committees.
(A) Every committee in which there are Members of
Parliament is a Parliamentary Committee.
(B) It works under the direction of the Speaker of the Lok
Sabha / Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
(C) It is appointed or elected by the House or nominated
by the Speaker/Chairman.
(D) It submits its report to the President of India.
(E) It has a secretariat provided by the Lok Sabha/Rajya
Sabha Secretariat.
book_questions.explanation_en:
A Parliamentary Committee must be
appointed or elected by the House or nominated by the
Speaker/Chairman, work under their direction, and have a
secretariat provided by the Parliament. They submit their
reports to the House or the Speaker/Chairman, not the
President. Not every committee with MPs is a
parliamentary committee (e.g., consultative committees).

book_questions.question_en:
How long can the Vice-President act as President,
when the office of President falls vacant?
book_questions.explanation_en:
According to Article 62(2) of the Indian
Constitution, when a vacancy in the office of the President
occurs, an election to fill the vacancy must be held within
six months. The Vice-President can act as President for a
maximum period of six months, during which a new
President must be elected.

book_questions.question_en:
Which of the following are the exclusive powers of
the Lok Sabha?
A. Introduction of the money bill
B. Ratification of the declaration of emergency
C. To pass a motion of no-confidence against the council
of ministers
D. To impeach the President
book_questions.explanation_en:
A Money Bill (A) can only be introduced in
the Lok Sabha. A no-confidence motion (C) against the
council of ministers can also only be introduced and
passed in the Lok Sabha. Ratification of emergency (B)
requires the approval of both houses, and impeachment of
the President (D) can be initiated in either house.
Therefore, A and C are exclusive powers of the Lok Sabha.

Which of the following is not a mechanism for

book_questions.explanation_en:
No-Confidence Motion, Calling Attention
Motion and Censure Motion are mechanisms through
which Parliament exercises control and scrutiny over the
executive. A Privilege Motion primarily concerns a breach
of parliamentary privilege rather than being a direct
mechanism of legislative control over the executive.

Legislative Council as an Indian National Congress
candidate representing Calcutta University. When the
Congress decided to boycott the legislature the following
year, he resigned but was subsequently re-elected as an
independent candidate.

book_questions.explanation_en:
Co-operative federalism in India has been

Union and States in economic and developmental matters

The compulsions of developmental finance, requiring
states to depend on central grants, also necessitate
cooperation (C).

book_questions.question_en:
The Supreme Court Of India in its order dated 24th
August 2017 in Justice. K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd) vs Union of
India declared that:
A. The right to privacy is protected as an intrinsic part of
the right to life and personal liberty under Article 21 and as
a part of the freedoms.
B. The Union government must amend the Constitution
and add a provision for the right to privacy.
C. The right to privacy is protected by Article 14(equality
before the law), Article 19 (Right to freedom), Article 21(
Protection of life and personal liberty).

freedom of religion) and Article 14(Protection of interests
of minorities)

the establishment of a Federal Court, the separation of

Sindh and Orissa. The Chamber of Princes was established
in 1920, and separate electorates for Muslims were
introduced by the Act of 1909.

book_questions.question_en:
What was the main reason for the introduction of
Economic Reforms by Narasimha Rao and Manmohan
Singh Government?
options_en: Pressure exerted by IMF and World Bank
Under pressure of United States of America
Under Pressure of Indian Corporate Houses
book_questions.explanation_en:
The economic reforms of 1991 were
introduced against the background of a severe balance-
of-payments crisis, declining foreign exchange reserves,
high fiscal pressures and broader macroeconomic
difficulties. Although institutions such as the IMF and
World Bank played an important role in the reform
programme, the immediate and fundamental reason was
the critical condition of the Indian economy. Therefore,
option (3) is correct.

book_questions.question_en:
Among the following challenges to Indian
Democracy, which one is not related to Globalization:
(A) Rise of Religious fundamentalism
(B) Rise of Regionalism
(C) Politics of defection
(D) Rise of ethnic movements
book_questions.explanation_en:
The politics of defection (legislators
switching parties) is an internal political issue related to
party discipline and anti-defection laws. While
globalization can exacerbate religious fundamentalism,
regionalism, and ethnic movements by creating economic
disparities or cultural insecurities, it is not a direct cause of
defection.

book_questions.question_en:
Who refers to the new economic policy in 1991 as a
tipping point transformation?
book_questions.explanation_en:
Rahul Mukherji, in his works on India's
political economy, has characterized the 1991 economic
reforms as a "tipping point," a fundamental transformation
in India's development strategy.

book_questions.question_en:
What is the correct chronological sequence of the
below? Choose the right answers from the codes:
(A) Joint Parliamentary Committee on Reform of Electoral
law
(B) Goswami Committee on electoral Reforms
(C) Tarkunde Committee on Electoral Reforms
(D) Election Commission's campaign against
criminalization of politics.
book_questions.explanation_en:
The correct chronological order is: Tarkunde
Committee (1974-75), a JPC was formed (1971-72 but its
report came after Tarkunde), Goswami Committee (1990),
and the EC's major campaigns against criminalization
intensified from the mid-1990s onward.

Which of the following is/are correct about Rani
Gaidinliau?

book_questions.question_en:
Arrange the following regional political parties in
chronological order, as per their date of establishment.
(A) DMK
(B) Shiromani Akali Dal
(C) TDP
(D) Biju Janata Dal
book_questions.explanation_en:

book_questions.question_en:
The demand for new Konkan state includes the
districts which are part of:
options_en: Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu
book_questions.explanation_en:
The proposed Konkan state is associated
with the Konkan coastal region, which extends across parts
of Maharashtra, Goa and Karnataka. Therefore, option
(4) is the appropriate answer..

book_questions.question_en:
The positive role of political parties in India could be
understood as:
options_en:
Informing the political opinions and influence the
government
Observation of transformations in the rest of the world
book_questions.explanation_en:
Political parties perform several democratic
functions such as political representation, political
mobilisation, aggregation of interests, recruitment of
leaders and formation of governments. Collectively, these
functions contribute to the consolidation and expansion
of democracy. Option (3) describes one important
function of political parties but is narrower than the overall
positive role asked in the question.

title: Political Processes in India - Practice 04

book_questions.question_en:
What do political parties, pressure groups, public
opinion, popular movements have in common ?
book_questions.explanation_en:
While political parties aim to capture power,
pressure groups, public opinion, and movements are
primarily informal organizations of power. They exist
outside the formal state structure and aim to influence
government policy and articulate public demands without
necessarily seeking to form a government themselves.

book_questions.question_en:
Samvadini is related to which of the following
movements?
book_questions.explanation_en:
"Samvadini" is a Dalit feminist literary and
cultural forum created to provide a platform for Dalit
women writers to articulate their unique experiences of
caste and gender oppression.

book_questions.question_en:
Labour movements in India suffers from
A. Low membership
B. Weak finances
C. Multiplicity of union
D. Presence of differentiated organizational structures for
different classes of labor
options_en: A, B, C and D only
book_questions.explanation_en:
The Indian labour movement has historically
been plagued by several issues. These include low rates of
unionization or membership (A), financial weakness due to
low membership fees (B), and the fragmentation of the
movement into a multiplicity of unions, often affiliated with
different political parties (C), which prevents a united front.

book_questions.question_en:
Which one of the following Chief Ministers resigned as
a consequence of Report submitted by Lokayukta?
book_questions.explanation_en:
B. S. Yeddyurappa, then Chief Minister of
Karnataka, resigned in July 2011 following the Karnataka
Lokayukta report headed by Justice N. Santosh Hegde. The
report alleged large-scale illegal mining and corruption
involving the state administration. Therefore, option (4) is
correct.

B. Janata Dal

E. Pattali Makkal Katchi

for Democracy (1977) → Telugu Desam Party (1982) →
Janata Dal (1988) → Pattali Makkal Katchi (1989).
Therefore, the correct sequence is A, C, D, B, E.

book_questions.question_en:
The National Democratic Alliance under Narendra
Modi came to power for the second time in 2019, few
important events of NDA's second term under Modi were:
A. The Muslim women Protection of Rights on Marriage Bill
was passed in 2019
. B. The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act was
passed in 2019.
C. In 2021, Amendments to the Protection of Animals from
Sexual Offences Act were enacted.
D. The Jammu and Kashmir Re-organisation Act was
passed in 2018.
E. The Central Government diluted Article 370 of the
Constitution in 2022.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
book_questions.explanation_en:
Statement A is correct; the law criminalizing
instant Triple Talaq was passed in July 2019. Statement B is
correct; the Transgender Persons Act was passed in 2019.
The other statements contain chronological errors:
Statement D is incorrect because the J&K Reorganisation
Act was passed in August 2019, not 2018. Statement E is
incorrect because the abrogation/dilution of Article 370
happened simultaneously in August 2019, not in 2022.

book_questions.question_en:
With the reference to Indian Political System,
consider the following statements.
(A) India is a democracy
(B) It is a Republic
(C) It is a Monarchy
(D) It provides for universal adult franchise
book_questions.explanation_en:
India is the world's largest democracy (A) and
a Republic (B), meaning its head of state (the President) is
elected, not a hereditary monarch (C is incorrect). It
guarantees the right to vote to all adult citizens through
universal adult franchise (D).

book_questions.question_en:
According to the Election Commission for being
considered as a national party, a political party should
atleast have which of the following qualification?
(A) It secures at least six percent of valid votes polled in
any four or more states at a general election to the Lok
Sabha or to the Legislative Assembly
(B) It wins at least two percent of seats in the Lok Sabha
from at least three different states
(C) It is recognised as a state party in at least four states
(D) It is registered as a political party
book_questions.explanation_en:
To be recognized as a National Party, a party
must satisfy any one of the three conditions laid down by
the Election Commission: the 6% vote share in 4 states rule
(A), the 2% Lok Sabha seats from 3 states rule (B), or
recognition as a State Party in 4 states (C). Registration (D)
is a basic requirement for any party, not specific to national
status.

book_questions.explanation_en:
The primary defining characteristic of a
political party is its aim to contest elections in order to
capture and exercise political power by forming a
government. Other groups like pressure groups and
interest groups aim to influence policy from the outside.

book_questions.explanation_en:

Congress (INTUC) - 1947 (A); Ahmedabad Textile Labour
Association - 1920 (B); Bombay Mill Hands Association -
1890 (D). Thus, the correct order is C, A, B, D.

book_questions.question_en: Who gave the concept of “Congress System”?
book_questions.explanation_en:
The concept of the “Congress System” was
developed by political scientist Rajni Kothari to describe
the dominant position of the Indian National Congress in
the early decades after independence. Kothari argued that
the Congress functioned as a broad umbrella organisation
containing different social and political interests within
itself.

book_questions.question_en:
Who amongst these said, concerning castes in India,
""Every society gets encumbered with what is trivial, with
dead wood from the past, and with what is positively
perverse"".
book_questions.explanation_en:
This quote from Dr. B.R. Ambedkar's
"Annihilation of Caste" reflects his strong critique of the
caste system as an outdated and perverse social structure.

(B) Non Co-operation Movement
(C) Civil Disobedience Movement
(D) Total Revolution Movement
book_questions.explanation_en:
The correct chronological sequence is: Non-

Total Revolution Movement (a call given by Jayaprakash

book_questions.question_en:
Arrange the Preventive Detention Acts enacted by
Indian Parliament in a chronological order:
A. National Security Act (NSA)
B. Maintenance of Internal Security Act (MISA)
C. Prevention of Terrorism Act (POTA)
D. Conservation of Foreign Exchange and Prevention of
Smugglers Activities Act (COFEPOSA)
E. Preventive Detention Act (PDA)
Choose the correct answer:
book_questions.explanation_en:
The Preventive Detention Act (PDA) was
enacted in 1950, MISA in 1971, COFEPOSA in 1974, NSA
in 1980 and POTA in 2002. Thus, the correct chronological
order is E → B → D → A → C.

book_questions.question_en:
In which of the following cases it was decided by the
five judge bench of the Supreme Court that a Judge of the
Supreme Court or High Court can be prosecuted and
convicted for Criminal misconduct?
options_en: C. Ravichandran v. Justice A. M. Bhattacharjee
K. Veeraswami v. Union of India
Sarojini Ramaswamy v. Union of India
book_questions.explanation_en:
In K. Veeraswami v. Union of India (1991), the
Supreme Court held that judges of the Supreme Court and
High Courts are not completely immune from criminal
prosecution. However, prosecution against a sitting judge
requires prior sanction from the appropriate authority.

The provision of two separate commissions for
Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes was provided in
the Constitution by:

Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes

National Commission for Scheduled Castes (Article
338) and the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes

book_questions.question_en:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as
Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R
Assertion A: Swami Sahajanand Saraswati formed the Bihar
Provincial Kisan Sabha in 1929 to mobilize peasant
grievances against Zamindari attacks on their occupancy
rights.
Reason R: At Lucknow Session of the Congress in 1936, the
All India Kisan Sabha was formed with Swami Sahajanand
Saraswati as its president.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most
appropriate answer from the options given below:
options_en:
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct
explanation of A

Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct
explanation of A
A is correct but R is not correct
A is not correct but R is correct
book_questions.explanation_en:
Assertion (A) is a true historical fact. Swami
Sahajanand Saraswati indeed formed the Bihar Provincial
Kisan Sabha (BPKS) in 1929 to organize peasants against
the oppressive Zamindari system. Reason (R) is also a true
fact. The All India Kisan Sabha (AIKS) was formed later in
1936, with him as the first president. However, R does not
explain A. The formation of a national body in 1936 cannot
be the reason or explanation for the formation of a
provincial body seven years earlier in 1929. Therefore, both
statements are independently correct.

book_questions.question_en:
Which of the following are the issues of debate in
electoral politics?
A. Electronic voting machine
B. One nation, one election
C. Single-member election commission
D. Introduction of the two-children norm for eligibility to
contest local elections
book_questions.explanation_en:
The reliability of EVMs (A), the proposal for
simultaneous 'One Nation, One Election' (B), and the
imposition of a two-child norm for local elections (D) are
all frequent and prominent topics of debate in
contemporary Indian electoral politics. A single-member
election commission (C) is not a current major point of
debate, as the multi-member format is well-established.

book_questions.question_en:
Which of the following are related to electoral
reform in India?
(A) Dinesh Goswami Committee
(B) Indrajit Gupta Committee
(C) Tarkunde Committee
(D) Santhanam Committee
book_questions.explanation_en:
The Dinesh Goswami Committee (1990), the
Indrajit Gupta Committee on State Funding of Elections
(1998), and the Tarkunde Committee (1974-75) were all
major committees that made significant recommendations
on electoral reforms in India. The Santhanam Committee
(1962-64) was focused on the prevention of corruption.

book_questions.question_en:
Which of the following does NOT characterise
electoral politics in India today?
options_en: Stabilization of the Congress dominance system
Increase in the scope of electoral choices of voters
book_questions.explanation_en:
The era of "Congress dominance" refers to
the first few decades after independence. Since the late
1980s, Indian politics has been characterized by a multi-
party system, the rise of coalition governments, and an
increase in electoral choices, marking the end, not the
stabilization, of the Congress-dominant system.

book_questions.question_en: Narasimha Rao fought and won elections from:
book_questions.explanation_en:
Former Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao
had a unique distinction of representing three different
states in the Lok Sabha during his political career:
Maharashtra: He won from the Ramtek constituency in the
1984 and 1989 general elections. Andhra Pradesh: After

assuming the office of Prime Minister in 1991, he
contested and won a by-election from Nandyal with a
record-breaking margin. Odisha (Orissa): In the 1996
general elections, he contested and won from the
Berhampur constituency.

"The Indian Paradox: Essays in Indian Politics"

book_questions.question_en:
Given below are two statements: One is labelled as
Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion (A): Pressure groups are involved in politics and
policy making process in India through direct and indirect
means.
Reasons (R): They aspire to come to power to achieve
their goals.
options_en:
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct
explanation of (A)

Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct
explanation of (A)
book_questions.explanation_en:
Pressure groups absolutely try to influence
politics and policy-making through various means (A is
true). However, the defining characteristic that
distinguishes a pressure group from a political party is that
they do not aspire to come to power themselves; they only
seek to influence those in power (R is false).

book_questions.question_en:
Who was the first Non-Congress Chief Minister of
Karnataka?
book_questions.explanation_en:
In the 1983 state assembly elections, the
Janata Party successfully defeated the Indian National
Congress in Karnataka. Following this historic victory,
Ramakrishna Hegde was sworn in as the first non-Congress
Chief Minister of the state. Other options: E.M.S.
Namboodripad was the first Chief Minister of Kerala. S.R.
Bommai and H.D. Deve Gowda also served as non-
Congress Chief Ministers of Karnataka later on, succeeding
Hegde's era.

book_questions.question_en:
Which university was the first to begin the protest
against the imposition of Emergency (1975)?
book_questions.explanation_en:
Following the declaration of the National
Emergency on June 25, 1975, by Prime Minister Indira
Gandhi, fundamental rights were suspended and
widespread arrests of opposition leaders occurred. The
University of Delhi (DU) emerged as the first major
academic epicenter of resistance. Its student unions and
faculty members immediately launched protests,
distributed underground pamphlets, and actively defied
press censorship. Prominent student leaders from DU at
the time (such as Arun Jaitley) were consequently
imprisoned under the Maintenance of Internal Security Act
(MISA).

→ Bureaucracy — 1922 (Weber) → The Giving of Orders

Incentives — 1938 (Chester Barnard). Therefore, the
correct sequence is C, B, A, D. The standard chronology o
organizational theory confirms these publication dates.

book_questions.question_en:
Match the LIST-I (Author) with LIST-II (Concepts):
LIST-I LIST-II
I. Principles of Scientific
A. Woodrow Wilson
Management
II. Importance of Study of
B. Frederick Taylor
Administration as
C. Luther Gulick III. Hierarchy of Needs
IV. Structure based
D. Abraham Maslow
Principles of Organisation
book_questions.explanation_en:
The correct associations are: Woodrow Wilson
advocated for the study of administration as a science in his
1887 essay. Frederick Taylor is the father of Scientific
Management. Luther Gulick is known for his structure-based
principles of organization (POSDCORB). Abraham Maslow
developed the Hierarchy of Needs theory.

book_questions.question_en:
Lyndall Urwick has identified eight principles of
organization. Which of the following is not part of those
eight.
book_questions.explanation_en:
Lyndall Urwick's principles of organization
include concepts like Correspondence, Span of Control, and
Coordination. "Generalization" is not one of his core,
explicitly listed principles.

book_questions.question_en:
Rensis Likert has identified four systems of
management on the basis of nature of authority and control
of organization. Arrange in ascending order of efficiency A.
Benevolent-Authority B. Consultative Leadership C.
Participative D. Exploitative Authoritative
book_questions.explanation_en:
Rensis Likert's four management systems,
arranged in ascending order of efficiency and democratic
participation, are: System 1: Exploitative Authoritative (least
efficient), System 2: Benevolent-Authoritative, System 3:
Consultative Leadership, and System 4: Participative (most
efficient). Therefore, the correct ascending order is D, A, B, C.

focus: Human relations, informal organization and behavioural approaches
title: Public Administration - Practice 03

book_questions.question_en:
Which of the following is/are correct:
(A) Structural approach focuses on economy and efficiency.
(B) Human Relation approach deals with the relationship
among the people working in organisation.
(C) Behavioural approach emphasises on the study of the
development aspect of the administration.
(D) Political economy approach emphasises on the
application of economic methods and models of political
problem
book_questions.explanation_en:
The classical structural approach emphasizes
principles like economy and efficiency (A). The Human
Relations approach focuses on the social and psychological
factors of people at work (B). The Political Economy approach
applies economic reasoning to political problems (D). The
Behavioural approach focuses on the actual behavior of
individuals in organizations, not specifically the
"development aspect" (C is less accurate).

book_questions.question_en:
Which of the following statements is incorrect about
the "Human Relations Theory"?
options_en: Organization is to be viewed as a social system
Workers are human beings with all humanly attributes

Informal elements do not play an important role in the
overall organizational output

Organization has social ethics, instead of individual
ethics
book_questions.explanation_en:
The Human Relations Theory, which originated
from the Hawthorne experiments, fundamentally argues that
informal social elements are critically important. It found that
social norms, group dynamics, and employee morale
(informal elements) often have a greater impact on
productivity than formal rules or physical conditions.
Therefore, the statement that they do not play an important
role is incorrect.

book_questions.question_en:
Which of the following thinkers recognized the
significance of informal groups in promoting organizational
development?
book_questions.explanation_en:
Elton Mayo is closely associated with the
Human Relations School of organizational theory. His
studies, particularly the Hawthorne studies, demonstrated
the importance of informal groups, social relationships,
morale and employee attitudes in organizational
performance. This challenged the purely mechanical
approach of classical theorists such as Taylor and Fayol.

book_questions.question_en:
Consider the following ideas associated with Douglas
McGregor and choose the correct answer:
(A) Theory X: The alternate assumptions of integration and
self-control
(B) Theory Y: The coercive compulsions
(C) Scanlon Plan
(D) The Human Side of the Enterprise
(E) Linking Pin Model
book_questions.explanation_en:
Douglas McGregor is most famous for his book
The Human Side of the Enterprise (D), where he proposed
Theory X and Theory Y. He was also a proponent of the
Scanlon Plan (C), a gain-sharing program. Statements A and
B incorrectly swap the descriptions of Theory X (coercive)
and Theory Y (integration/self-control). The Linking Pin
model is associated with Rensis Likert.

focus: Systems, decision-making, bounded rationality and ecological approaches
title: Public Administration - Practice 04

book_questions.question_en:
Match List I with List II
List I List Il
A. Decision Making I. Fred Riggs
B. Ecological Approach II. Edward Wiedner
C. New Public III. Herbert Simon
Administration
D. Development IV. Minnowbrook
Administration Conference 1968
book_questions.explanation_en:
This matches concepts and schools of though
to their proponents. Decision Making theory is famously
associated with Herbert Simon. The Ecological Approach in
public administration was pioneered by Fred Riggs. New
Public Administration gained its identity from the
Minnowbrook Conference of 1968. Developmen
Administration is a field with many contributors, with Edward
Weidner being a key early figure.

book_questions.question_en:
Which of the following idea(s)/concept(s) is/are given
by Chester Barnard?
A. Acceptance theory of authority and Zone of Indifference
B. Contribution satisfaction equilibrium
C. Functions of the executive
D. Bounded rationality
book_questions.explanation_en:
Chester Barnard is famous for his "Acceptance
Theory of Authority" and the related "Zone of Indifference"
(A), the concept of "Contribution-Satisfaction Equilibrium"
(B), and his book "The Functions of the Executive" (C).
"Bounded Rationality" (D) is a concept developed by Herbert
Simon.

book_questions.question_en:
Which of the following statements best describe New
Public Management? There is a shift:
A. In emphasis from policy making to management skills
B. From stress on process to a stress on output
C. From uniform to inclusive public service
D. From orderly hierarchies to a competitive mode
Choose the correct answer:
book_questions.explanation_en:
New Public Management (NPM) emphasizes
managerial skills, measurable outputs, performance and
competition. It represents a shift away from traditional
bureaucratic procedures and rigid hierarchies toward results-
oriented and competitive forms of administration. Statement
C is not a defining shift of NPM. Therefore, A, B and D are
correct.

book_questions.question_en: Ecological approach is the key to the understanding of:
book_questions.explanation_en:
The ecological approach, particularly
associated with Fred W. Riggs, studies public administration
in relation to its social, economic, political and cultura
environment. It is therefore especially important fo
understanding Comparative Public Administration, where
administrative systems are studied in their respective
environmental contexts.
: Source: UGC NET June 2026

focus: Development administration and comparative public administration
title: Public Administration - Practice 05

book_questions.question_en:
Which of the following are correct about Comparative
Public Administration (CPA)?
A. CPA focuses on the structure, process, behaviour, roles
and impact of public administrative system at the
international level.
B. Comparative Administrative Group (CAG) was set up in
1963.
C. CAG was funded by American Political Science
Association.
D. F.W. Riggs was the chairman of CAG from its inception till
the end of 1970.
book_questions.explanation_en:
CPA is the cross-cultural study of public
administration (A). The Comparative Administration Group
(CAG) was a key driver of the movement, chaired by Fred
Riggs (D). It was established in 1960 (formally 1963 as a
committee of ASPA) (B). It was funded by the Ford
Foundation, not the American Political Science Association (C
is incorrect).

book_questions.question_en:
Who is called the father of 'Comparative Public
Administration'?
book_questions.explanation_en:
Fred W. Riggs is widely regarded as the
"father" of Comparative Public Administration. His
pioneering work, particularly his ecological approach and
models like the 'Agraria-Industria' and 'Fused-Prismatic-
Diffracted' models, laid the theoretical foundation for the
systematic comparison of administrative systems across
different cultures.

book_questions.question_en:
Who wrote the book 'Development Administration:
Concepts, Goals, Methods'?
book_questions.explanation_en:
George F. Gant is credited with writing this
influential book. He was a key figure in the field of
development administration, and his work helped define its
scope, focusing on the administration of development
programs in developing countries.

: Source: UGC NET June 2025

book_questions.question_en:
Who is the author of The Study of Public
Administration?
book_questions.explanation_en:
While Woodrow Wilson wrote the essay "The
Study of Administration," the book titled "The Study of Public
Administration" (1955) was authored by Dwight Waldo. It is a
key text that critiques the politics-administration dichotomy
and examines the philosophical underpinnings of the field.

focus: New Public Administration, social equity and Minnowbrook
title: Public Administration - Practice 06

book_questions.question_en:
The rise and growth of the concept of New Public
Administration can be traced to:
A. Honey Report on Higher Education for Public Services –
1967
B. Minnowbrook Conference II – 1988
C. Philadelphia Conference on the Theory and Practice of
Public Administration – 1967
D. Public Administration in a Time of Turbulence - 1971
book_questions.explanation_en:
The intellectual ferment leading to New Public
Administration (NPA) included the Honey Report (A) and the
Philadelphia Conference (C), which highlighted the
shortcomings of traditional PA. NPA's key ideas were
consolidated in the book "Public Administration in a Time of
Turbulence" (D), edited by Dwight Waldo, which followed the
first Minnowbrook Conference (1968). Minnowbrook II (B)
was a later event that reviewed the field.

book_questions.question_en:
Indian Institute of Public Administration was set up to
serve as a "Think Tank" to the Government of India, in which
year?
book_questions.explanation_en:
The Indian Institute of Public Administration
(IIPA) was established in March 1954. Its creation was based
on the recommendation of a survey conducted by American
public administration expert Paul H. Appleby, with the aim of
advancing the study and practice of public administration in
India.

book_questions.question_en:
Who said that "Public Administration is the
accomplishment of politically determined objectives"?
book_questions.explanation_en:
This definition is attributed to Marshall E.
Dimock and Gladys O. Dimock. Their view emphasizes the
implementation aspect of public administration, seeing it as
the tool for carrying out the goals and objectives decided
upon through the political process, highlighting the close
relationship between politics and administration.

book_questions.question_en:
Identify the correct thinkers/ideas.
(A) Henri Fayol - Management Process School
(B) Max Weber - Legal-Irrational Authority
(C) Mary Parker Follett - Idea of Constructive Conflict
(D) Elton Mayo - Great Illumination Experiment
(E) Chester Barnard - Spiritual father of the Social System
School
book_questions.explanation_en:
Henri Fayol is a key figure in the Management
Process School. Mary Parker Follett introduced the concept
of constructive conflict. The Hawthorne Experiments, with
which Elton Mayo is associated, included the Illumination
Experiments. Chester Barnard is often considered the
spiritual father of the Social System School. Max Weber's
concept was Legal-Rational Authority, not irrational, making
statement (B) incorrect.

focus: New Public Management, public choice and reforms under liberalization
title: Public Administration - Practice 07

book_questions.question_en:
Patrick Dunleavy has enumerated which of the three
key components of New Public Management ?
options_en: Conservation, displacement of goals and conflict
book_questions.explanation_en:
Patrick Dunleavy, a prominent analyst of New
Public Management, identified three core components of the
movement: Disaggregation (breaking down large public
bureaucracies into smaller, specialized agencies),
Competition (introducing market-style competition between
public agencies and with the private sector), and
Incentivisation (using performance targets and financial
incentives to drive efficiency).

book_questions.question_en:
Mc Gregor in his celebrated text, The Human Side of
the Enterprise has given his famous "theoretical
assumptions". Which of the following are the correct
assumptions?
A. The average human being, with relatively little ambition,
prefers to be directed and wishes to avoid responsibility.
Security is the main concern
B. The average human being learns under proper conditions
not only to accept but to seek responsibility
C. The average human being has an innate antipathy to
work, which he will avoid, if he can
D. "Best management is a true science"
book_questions.explanation_en:
Douglas McGregor proposed two sets of
assumptions: Theory X and Theory Y. Statements (A) and (C)
are core assumptions of the pessimistic Theory X. Statement
(B) is a core assumption of the optimistic Theory Y.
Statement (D) is more aligned with Frederick Taylor's
Scientific Management, not McGregor's work. The question
asks for correct assumptions from his text, and A, B, and C all
are.

book_questions.question_en:
The first Administrative Reforms Commission was
established in-
book_questions.explanation_en:
The Government of India constituted the First
Administrative Reforms Commission (1st ARC) on January 5,
1966, to thoroughly examine the public administration
system of the country and recommend reforms. It was
initially chaired by Morarji Desai. Later, when Desai became
the Deputy Prime Minister, K. Hanumanthaiya became its
chairman. The 1st ARC is most famous for recommending
the establishment of the institutions of Lokpal and Lokayukta
in India.

book_questions.question_en:
Who contended that "we are concerned only with
finding a choice mechanism that will lead it to pursue a
"satisficing" path?
book_questions.explanation_en:
This quote relates to the concept of "bounded
rationality," which was introduced by Herbert Simon. He
argued that decision-makers in organizations do not have
the capacity to be perfectly rational. Instead, they "satisfice"--
-they search for a solution that is "good enough" or
satisfactory, rather than the optimal one.

focus: Leadership and motivation theories: Maslow, Herzberg, McGregor and established models
title: Public Administration - Practice 08

book_questions.question_en:
Match List I with List II:
Theory/Concept Thinker
A. Constructive Conflict I. Frederic Herzberg
B. Acceptance Theory of II. Abraham Maslow
authority and Zonal
Indifference
C. Hierarchy of Needs III. Chester I. Barnard
D. Hygiene-Motivation IV. Mary Parker Follett
theory
book_questions.explanation_en:
"Constructive Conflict" is a concept by Mary
Parker Follett. The "Acceptance Theory of Authority" and
"Zone of Indifference" are from Chester Barnard. The
"Hierarchy of Needs" was developed by Abraham Maslow.
The "Motivation-Hygiene Theory" was proposed by Frederick
Herzberg.

book_questions.question_en:
Frederick Herzberg is famous for which one of the
following theories?
book_questions.explanation_en:
Frederick Herzberg is a key figure in
management and motivation theory. He is famous for his
"Two-Factor Theory" (also known as the Motivator-Hygiene
Theory), which distinguishes between factors that cause job
satisfaction (motivators) and factors that cause job
dissatisfaction (hygiene factors).

book_questions.question_en:
Match List I with List II
List I List II
A. Frederick Taylor I. Functions of the Executive
B. Peter Drucker II. Mental Revolution
C. Chester Bernard III. Management by
Objectives
D. Abraham Maslow IV. Motivation
book_questions.explanation_en:
This matches thinkers with their key concepts.
Frederick Taylor called for a "Mental Revolution" in both
management and workers. Peter Drucker is credited with
developing "Management by Objectives" (MBO). Chester
Barnard wrote the influential book The Functions of the
Executive. Abraham Maslow is famous for his "Hierarchy of
Needs" theory of motivation.

book_questions.question_en:
Hierarchy of needs, Theory X and Theory Y, Hygiene
theory are related to theories of:
book_questions.explanation_en:
These are important theories of motivation.
Abraham Maslow proposed the Hierarchy of Needs; Douglas
McGregor developed Theory X and Theory Y; and Frederick
Herzberg developed the Two-Factor or Hygiene-Motivation
Theory. All three explain factors influencing human
motivation and behaviour in organisations.

focus: Organizational communication, Barnard, information and coordination
title: Public Administration - Practice 09

book_questions.question_en:
Who wrote the famous book 'Men who Manage' on
aspect of organizational life ?
book_questions.explanation_en:
The book Men Who Manage (1959) is a classic
sociological study of organizational life written by Melville
Dalton. Through his covert participant observation, he
highlighted the informal structures and power struggles that
exist within formal organizations.

book_questions.question_en:
Arrange the following thinkers in chronologic order of
their birth year
(A) Chester Barnard
(B) M.P. Follet
(C) Henri Fayol
(D) Dwight Waldo
book_questions.explanation_en:
The approximate birth years are: Henri Fayol
(1841), M.P. Follett (1868), Chester Barnard (1886), and
Dwight Waldo (1913).

book_questions.question_en:
Which one of the following orders falls under the
"zone of indifference" propounded by Chester Barnard?
options_en: Those which will be clearly unacceptable

Those which are on neutral line i.e. either just acceptable
or just unacceptable
Order that fails intentionally in an obligation
book_questions.explanation_en:
Chester Barnard's "zone of indifference" refers
to the range of orders that a subordinate will accept from a
superior without question. These are orders that are
perceived as legitimate and fall within the expected scope of
the job, and are therefore "unquestionably acceptable."

book_questions.question_en:
Performance budget reflects how well a government
entity is meeting its goals and objectives. Which of the
following are the central point of Performance Budgeting?
A. It requires the establishment of performance levels and
the collection of information
B. The amount of work that is done is measured
C. The quality or the results of that work is measured
D. This impacts how much money a department will receive
in the future
options_en: A, B, C and D only
book_questions.explanation_en:
Performance budgeting links funding to
measurable outcomes. It involves establishing performance
targets (A), measuring the quantity of work or outputs (B),
measuring the quality or outcomes of that work (C), and
using this performance data to inform future budget
allocations (D). All four are central aspects of this budgeting
approach.

focus: Follett, conflict management, integration and management by objectives
title: Public Administration - Practice 10

book_questions.question_en:
Mary Parker Follett suggested certain styles of handling
conflict. They are:
A. Domination, Compromise and Integration
B. Adjustment, Bargain and Discussion
C. Avoidance and Suppression
D. Study, Understand and Explore
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
book_questions.explanation_en:
Mary Parker Follett identified domination,
compromise and integration as major ways of dealing with
conflict. She also discussed avoidance and suppression as
ways in which conflict may be dealt with, although she
strongly preferred constructive integration. Therefore, among
the given combinations, A and C only is appropriate

book_questions.question_en:
Which of the following are the advanced ideas of
Mary Follett?
A. Functional Foremanship
B. Constructive Conflict
C. Zone of Acceptance
D. Integration
book_questions.explanation_en:
Mary Parker Follett was a pioneering thinker in
organizational theory. Her key ideas include "Constructive
Conflict," viewing conflict not as something to be suppressed
but as an opportunity for growth, and "Integration," he
preferred method for resolving conflict where a new solution
is created that satisfies the desires of all parties. Functiona
Foremanship is Taylor's idea, and Zone of Acceptance
belongs to Chester Barnard.

book_questions.question_en:
Management by objectives was the key idea put
forward by Peter Drucker in:
book_questions.explanation_en:
Management guru Peter Drucker first
introduced the concept of Management by Objectives (MBO)
in his influential 1954 book, "The Practice of Management."
MBO is a management model that aims to improve
organizational performance by clearly defining objectives
that are agreed upon by both management and employees.

book_questions.question_en:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as
Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R: Assertion A
The assumptions of Theory 'Y' is that integration of behaviour
is the key process in management Reason R: Theory 'Y'
results in the creation of conditions conducive for the
members to achieve their own goals by directing their efforts
towards the success of the enterprise.
options_en:
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of
A

Both A and R are true but R is not the correct
explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but B is true
book_questions.explanation_en:
Douglas McGregor's Theory Y assumes
employees are self-motivated. The key management process
is therefore the integration of individual and organizationa
goals (A). By creating the right conditions, managemen
allows employees to achieve their own goals by working
towards the organization's success (R). Thus, R correctly
explains A.

focus: Integrated organizational theory, accountability, administrative ethics and governance applications
title: Public Administration - Practice 11

book_questions.question_en:
Two important institutions that contributed
significantly to the Development of Administrative theory and
practice are
book_questions.explanation_en:
Historically, the Roman Catholic Church and
military organizations were among the earliest large-scale
institutions to develop complex administrative structures and
hierarchies, influencing modern administrative theory.

book_questions.question_en:
Abraham Maslow's theory of needs in the hierarchy
consists of:
(A) Physiological needs
(B) Esteem needs
(C) Security needs
(D) Self-actualisation needs
(E) Spiritual needs
book_questions.explanation_en:
Abraham Maslow's famous hierarchy of needs
includes five levels: Physiological needs (food, water),
Security/Safety needs, Social needs (love/belonging), Esteem
needs (respect, status), and Self-actualisation needs
(achieving one's full potential). While self-actualization can
have a spiritual dimension, "spiritual needs" is not one of the
formal categories in his model.

book_questions.question_en:
System Theory focuses on the study of organisation as
a :
book_questions.explanation_en:
Drawing from the work of thinkers like Cheste
Barnard, the Systems Theory views an organization as an
open, cooperative or collaborative system. It emphasizes the
interrelationship of its parts and its interaction with the

external environment to achieve common goals, rather than
seeing it merely as a closed or purely hierarchical structure.

Match List I with List II

theory of action

Politics
