Science
book_questions.explanation_en:
(A) "Political Science: A Philosophical Analysis"
was written by Vernon Van Dyke. (B) "Political Science and
the Theory of Action" is associated with John G. Gunnell. (C)
"The American Science of Politics" is a famous work by
Bernard Crick. (D) Heinz Eulau wrote extensively on different
"segments" of political science.

unit: Governance and Public Policy in India

title: Governance and Public Policy in India - Practice 01

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en:
In which year then Viceroy of India passed a
resolution of local self-government which led the
democratic forms of Municipal Governance in India?
book_questions.explanation_en:
Lord Ripon, the Viceroy of India, issued a
landmark resolution in 1882 regarding local self-
government. This resolution is widely considered the
'Magna Carta' of local self-government in India as it laid
the foundational principles for democratic municipal
governance and rural boards. Because of this historic
initiative, Lord Ripon is hailed as the "Father of Local Self-
Government in India."

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en: Identify the correct statement for Good Governance.
options_en: Governance which is not good is bad governance.
Good Governance is about processes and structures.

Transparency and Accountability are the hallmark of

Good Governance.

Good Governance depends upon the sweet will of the
people in power.
book_questions.explanation_en:
Good governance is defined by key principles
that make systems work for the people. Among its most
crucial elements are transparency (clarity in decision-
making) and accountability (answerability of officials to the
public). The other statements are either tautological,
incomplete, or incorrect.

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en:
A Civil Society eco system usually includes within its
ambit
(A) Non Profit Organisation
(B) Online groups
(C) Religious Leaders

(D) Legislature
book_questions.explanation_en:
Civil society exists in the space between the
family, the state, and the market. It includes non-profit
organizations (A), online advocacy groups (B), and
community/religious leaders (C) acting in the public
sphere. The legislature (D) is a formal institution of the
state and is therefore not part of civil society.

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: U.N. has defined 12 Pillars of good
governance.
Statement II: SDG 14 is directly linked to improvement in
governance.
options_en: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
book_questions.explanation_en:
The UN and other bodies have identified key
characteristics of good governance, but not a fixed list of
"12 Pillars" (Statement I is false). SDG 16 (not 14) is directly
focused on "Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions" and is
linked to improving governance (Statement II is false as it

mentions the wrong SDG number).

unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
focus: Accountability: legislative, executive, budgetary and judicial control
title: Governance and Public Policy in India - Practice 02

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en:
Which of the following are the tools of executive
control over administration?
(A) Civil Service Code
(B) Staff agencies
(C) Budget
(D) Ordinances
(E) suits against public officials.
options_en: A, B, C, D and E only
B, C, D and E only
A, B C and D only
book_questions.explanation_en:
The executive controls the administration
through the civil service code (A), staff agencies like the
Cabinet Secretariat (B), control over the budget (C), and the
power to issue ordinances (D). Suits against officials (E) are
a form of judicial control.

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en:
Which of the following statements is/are correct
regarding accountability and control over administration?
(A) Administrative Accountability may refer to the legal
and hierarchical locus of Responsibility
(B) Administrative responsibility has ethical and normative

connotations
(C) Administrative responsibility implies that the public
officials will adhere to the explicit and implicit values of
proper administration and policy.
book_questions.explanation_en:
All three statements are correct.
Accountability refers to formal, hierarchical, and legal
mechanisms (A). Responsibility has a broader, ethical
dimension (B), which implies adherence to professional
values (C).

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en:
Which of the following statements is/are correct
regarding accountability and control over administration?1
(A) Administrative Accountability may refer to the legal
and hierarchical locus of Responsibility

unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
focus: Administrative reforms, administrative culture, integrity and corruption
title: Governance and Public Policy in India - Practice 03

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en:
Given below are two statements
Statement I: The 2nd Administrative Reforms Commission
in its Seventh Report entitled "Capacity Building for Conflict
Resolution" dealt with illegal immigration into the North
East and drew attention towards having a multi-purpose
national identity card for citizens
Statement II: Lokvani is a public-private partnership
project at Sitapur District in Uttar Pradesh which was
initiated in December, 2009
options_en: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
book_questions.explanation_en:
Statement I is true; the 2nd ARC's report on
conflict resolution did address issues in the North East and
recommended a multi-purpose national identity card.
Statement II is false; the Lokvani project in Sitapur was a

pioneering e-governance initiative, but it was started in
November 2004, not December 2009.

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en:
The government set up a third committee on police
reforms under the stewardship of former Union Home
Secretary K. Padmanabhaiah in the year:
book_questions.explanation_en:
The Ministry of Home Affairs constituted the
Committee on Police Reforms under the chairmanship of K.
Padmanabhaiah in the year 2000. Its mandate was to study,
examine, and recommend solutions for the modernization
of the police force, improving police-public relations,
reducing political interference, and restructuring police
recruitment and training.

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en:
The G.V.K. Rao Committee was appointed by the
Planning Commission to review the existing administrative
arrangements for rural development in:
book_questions.explanation_en:
The G.V.K. Rao Committee was appointed in
1985 by the Planning Commission. Its primary objective
was to examine the administrative structures for rural
development and poverty alleviation programs.
: Source: UGC NET June 2025

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en:
Which of the following are included in PM Modi's
vision of Developed India as 'Panchpran'?
(A) Atmnirbhav Bharat
(B) Goal of Developed India
(C) Security
(D) Unity and sense of duty
(E) Integrity.
book_questions.explanation_en:
The "Panch Pran" (Five Pledges) are: 1. The
goal of a developed India (B); 2. Remove any trace of a
colonial mindset; 3. Take pride in our roots; 4. Unity and
solidarity (D); and 5. Sense of duty among citizens (D).

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en:
Which of the following statements are true relating to
Consumer Protection Act 2019?
A. Provides for improved protection for consumers involved
in online transactions.
B. The definition of ‘advertisement’ has been widened.
C. The Act excludes e-commerce transactions from its
scope.
D. A Central Consumer Protection Authority has been
established.
Choose the correct answer:
book_questions.explanation_en:
The Consumer Protection Act, 2019
expanded consumer protection to cover the digital and e-
commerce environment, strengthened protection against
misleading advertisements, and established the Central
Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA). Therefore,
statements A, B and D are correct. Statement C is false
because e-commerce transactions are covered by the Act.

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en:
New provisions under the Consumer Protection Act
include: (A) Product liability (B) E-commerce (C) Mediation
(D) Unfair contract
book_questions.explanation_en:
The Consumer Protection Act, 2019,
introduced several new provisions to strengthen consumer
rights. These include holding manufacturers and sellers
liable for defective products (product liability), specific rules
for e-commerce, provisions for settling disputes through
mediation, and declaring unilateral and unfair contracts
void.

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en:
Arrange the following legislative acts in
chronological orders:
(A) Right to Information Act
(B) Consumer Protection Act
(C) Right to Education Act
(D) Lokpal and Lokayukta Act
book_questions.explanation_en:
The correct chronological order of enactment
is: Consumer Protection Act (1986), Right to Information

Act (2005), Right to Education Act (2009), and Lokpal and
Lokayukta Act (2013).

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en:
Arrange the Acts chronologically:
A. National Food Security Act
B. Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act
C. Freedom of Information Act
D. Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and other
Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act
E. Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee
Act
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
book_questions.explanation_en:
The MGNREGA Act was enacted in 2005, the
Freedom of Information Act in 2002, the National Food
Security Act in 2013, the Muslim Women (Protection of
Rights on Marriage) Act in 2019, and the Aadhaar Act in
2016. Therefore, the strictly chronological order is C → E →
A → D → B.

Indian states enacted their respective Lokayukta Acts

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en: The first Lokpal bill was introduced in Parliament.
book_questions.explanation_en:
The first Lokpal Bill was introduced in the Lok
Sabha in 1968, based on the recommendations of the First
Administrative Reforms Commission. However, the bill
lapsed with the dissolution of the Lok Sabha.

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en:
Who among the following proposed the concept of
Constitutional Ombudsman in Parliament in India?
book_questions.explanation_en:
The idea of a Lokpal (Ombudsman) was first
introduced in the Indian Parliament by the then Law
Minister, Ashok Kumar Sen, in the early 1960s.

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en:
Match List I with List II
List I List II
A. E-Governance I. 73rd Amendment Act
B. Panchayati Raj II. NeGP
C. Redressal of III. 2009
Grievances
D. Right to Education IV. Ombudsman
book_questions.explanation_en:
This matches concepts to their associated
acts or institutions. E-Governance in India is driven by the
National e-Governance Plan (NeGP). Panchayati Raj
institutions were given constitutional status by the 73rd
Amendment Act. The Ombudsman (like the Lokpal) is a key
institution for the Redressal of Grievances. The Right to
Education Act was enacted in 2009.

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en:
Arrange the organisations/institutions of Indian
Political System in chronological order according to the
year of their establishment:
A. Central Vigilance Commission
B. Planning Commission
C. Inter-State Council
D. NITI Aayog
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
book_questions.explanation_en:
The Planning Commission was established
in 1950, the Central Vigilance Commission in 1964, the
Inter-State Council in 1990, and NITI Aayog in 2015.
Therefore, the correct chronological order is B → A → C →
D.

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en:
Which organisation provides a robust
communication system and effective support for e-
governance in India?
book_questions.explanation_en:
The National Informatics Centre (NIC) is the
premier government institution that provides the ICT
infrastructure and services for e-governance initiatives
across all levels of government in India. It manages the
national data and communication network.

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en:
Which Committee was appointed by Janata
Government to review the working of th Party Panchayati
Raj Institutions ?
book_questions.explanation_en:
In December 1977, the Janata Party
government appointed a committee on Panchayati Raj
institutions under the chairmanship of Ashok Mehta. The
committee submitted its report in August 1978 and made
132 recommendations to revive and strengthen the
declining Panchayati Raj system in the country.

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en:
Arrange the following Committees related to

committees is: Working Group on Panchayats and Co-
operatives (A): S. D. Misra, 1961 Study Team on Nyaya-

Panchayati Raj Elections (C): K. Santhanam, 1965
Committee on Panchayati Raj Training Centres (D): G.
Ramachandran, 1966 Committee on Community
Development and Panchayati Raj (E): M. Ramakrishnayya,
1976

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en:
Which is the nodal agency to achieve Sustainable
Development Goals in India?
options_en: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
book_questions.explanation_en:
The NITI Aayog (National Institution for
Transforming India) has been designated as the nodal
agency for coordinating and monitoring the
implementation of the Sustainable Development Goals
(SDGs) in India.

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en:

The correct historical mapping of these

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en:
Arrange the following stages of Public Policy Process
in a sequential order.
(A) Policy Formulation
(B) Policy Evaluation
(C) Policy Adoption
(D) Policy Implementation

(E) Agenda Setting
book_questions.explanation_en:
The public policy cycle follows a logical
sequence: 1. Agenda Setting: Identifying a problem that
needs government action. 2. Policy Formulation:
Developing possible solutions or policy options. 3. Policy
Adoption: The government formally chooses and
legitimizes a policy. 4. Policy Implementation: Putting the
chosen policy into effect. 5. Policy Evaluation: Assessing the
effectiveness and impact of the policy.

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en:
Which of the following report is published by NITI
AAYOG?
book_questions.explanation_en:
The National Multidimensional Poverty Index
(MPI) for India is published by the NITI Aayog. The

Economic Survey is prepared by the Ministry of Finance,
and employment/unemployment data comes from the
National Statistical Office (NSO).

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en:
Which of the following institutes and bodies have an
important role to play in policy planning?
A. Indian Statistical Institute
B. National Council of Applied Economic Research
C. Comptroller and Auditor General
D. Council of Scientific and Industrial Research
book_questions.explanation_en:
The Indian Statistical Institute (ISI), the
National Council of Applied Economic Research (NCAER),
and the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR)
all provide crucial data, research, and technical inputs that
are vital for evidence-based policy planning. The
Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) is an auditing body
that comes into play after policies are implemented,
focusing on financial accountability, not initial planning.

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en:
Which among the following is the role of
representative according to John Wahlke?
(A) Trustee-deputy role
(B) Facilitator-neutral role
(C) District state or country role
(D) Revolutionary role
book_questions.explanation_en:
John Wahlke's famous study identified three
main roles: Trustee (uses own judgment), Delegate (follows
constituents' wishes), and Politico (balances both). The
options given are a simplification of this, with "Trustee-
deputy role" and "Facilitator-neutral role" best capturing
the essence of his typology.

"Social Structure and the Ruling Class" is

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en:
What is not included in 'Five E' approach in Policy
analysis?
book_questions.explanation_en:
The 'Five E's' framework for policy analysis
typically includes Effectiveness, Efficiency, Equity, Ethical
Considerations, and Economy. 'Evidences' is a crucial part
of analysis but is not one of the 'E's in this specific
framework.

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en:
Which of the following Schemes is/are launched by
the current Central Government?
(A) Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojna.
(B) Kisan Nyay Yojna.
(C) Pradhan Mantri Gareeb Kalyan Yojna.
(D) Meri Policy Mere Haath
book_questions.explanation_en:
Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY),
Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Yojana (PMGKY), and Meri
Policy Mere Haath are all schemes launched by the central
government under Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Kisan
Nyay Yojna was a scheme proposed by the Congress party.

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en:
On 2nd October 1959, who inaugurated Panchayat at
Nagaur?
book_questions.explanation_en:
On October 2, 1959 (coinciding with
Mahatma Gandhi's birth anniversary), India's first Prime
Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, formally inaugurated the three-
tier Panchayati Raj system in Nagaur district, Rajasthan.
This implementation was based on the recommendations
for "democratic decentralization" made by the Balwant Rai
Mehta Committee (1957). Rajasthan thereby became the
first state in independent India to implement the
Panchayati Raj system, followed shortly by Andhra Pradesh.

book_questions.explanation_en:
The launch years of these government

Samriddhi: 2021 (D) Inauguration of Kartavya Path: 2022

title: Governance and Public Policy in India - Practice 10

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en: What is the effects of globalization on food security?
options_en:
Wealthy countries subsidies and trade barrier make it
difficult for developing countries to take advantage of the
potential of globalization for advancing food security.

World Trade Organisation rules do not cover agriculture,
so globalisation really has no bearing on food Security.

Supermarket are so far the only way in which food and
agriculture have experienced globalization.

Developing countries need to create publicly owned
food reserves in order to realise the potential benefit.
book_questions.explanation_en:
A major critique of globalization's impact on
food security is that agricultural subsidies and protectionist
trade barriers in wealthy countries distort global markets,
making it difficult for farmers in developing countries to
compete, thus undermining their food security.

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en:
Who was the chairman of the 'Health Survey and
Development Committee' appointed in 1943 in India?
book_questions.explanation_en:
The Health Survey and Development
Committee, appointed by the Government of India in 1943,
is popularly known as the Bhore Committee after its
chairman, Sir Joseph Bhore. Its comprehensive 1946 report
laid out a blueprint for the development of public health
services in post-independence India.

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en:
Which of the following were/are wage development
and infrastructure development programmes?
A. Crash Scheme of Rural Employment
B. National Rural Employment Guarantee Programme
C. Rural Landless Employment Guarantee Programme
D. Changes in Agronomic Practices
book_questions.explanation_en:
The Crash Scheme for Rural Employment
(1971), the National Rural Employment Guarantee
Programme (NREGA, 2005), and the Rural Landless
Employment Guarantee Programme (RLEGP, 1983) were all
government initiatives aimed at providing employment
(wages) through the creation of durable community assets
(infrastructure) in rural areas. Changes in agronomic
practices (D) relate to agricultural techniques, not direct
wage programmes.

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en:
The National Commission for Women was set up in
which year?
book_questions.explanation_en:
The National Commission for Women (NCW)
was established in January 1992 as a statutory body under
the National Commission for Women Act, 1990. Its
mandate is to review the legal safeguards for women and
advise the government on policy matters.

: Source: UGC NET June 2025

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en: Advantages of social audit.
options_en:
Promotes collective decision making and sharing
responsibilities
book_questions.explanation_en:
A social audit is a process where the
community collectively monitors the implementation of a
program or policy. Its primary advantage is that it
empowers citizens, enhances transparency, and promotes
collective decision-making and shared responsibility
between the people and the administration.

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en:
RTI is a means of strengthening democracy due to :
(A) Openness
(B) Maintaining secrecy
(C) Transparency
(D) Bureautic redtapism
(E) Accountability
book_questions.explanation_en:
The Right to Information (RTI) strengthens
democracy by promoting Openness (A) in governance,
ensuring Transparency (C) in the functioning of public
authorities, and enforcing the Accountability (E) of the
government to the people. Maintaining secrecy (B) and
bureaucratic red-tapism (D) are the very problems that the
RTI Act seeks to overcome.

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en:
Given below are two statements: Statement I: social
Action and Social Reforms both have normative ends.
Statement II: social reform is only one field of social action.
The scope of social action is much wider.
options_en: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
book_questions.explanation_en:
Both social action and reform are driven by
normative goals (how society should be). Social action is a
broader concept that includes any organized effort to
address social problems, while social reform is a specific
type of social action. Therefore, the scope of social action is
wider.

book_questions.unit: Governance and Public Policy in India
book_questions.question_en:
Match List I with List II:
Place Jansunwai
A. Kot Kirana I. IVth Jan Sunwai
B. Bhim II. Ist Jan Sunwai
C. Vijapura III. IInd Jan Sunwai
D. Jawaja IV. IIIrd Jan Sunwai
book_questions.explanation_en:
This question traces the early sequence of
the historic Jan Sunwais (Public Hearings) organized by the
Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan (MKSS) in Rajasthan. The
first was in Kot Kirana, followed by Bhim, then Vijaypura,
and then Jawaja.
